title: Five Daily Prayers
objective: After this level you can explain how Muslims prepare for and perform salah five times a day facing Mecca, and why Friday prayer is special.
summary: Muslims pray at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and evening, after washing, facing the Kaaba in Mecca; on Friday the prayer after noon becomes a congregational prayer with sermons.

cards.headline: Five times a day, Muslims everywhere turn toward one building in Mecca.
cards.body: Which building, and how does a prayer unfold, from the first splash of water to the last bow?

cards.headline: Five set times
cards.body: The day's prayers have names: fajr at dawn, zuhr at midday, asr in the afternoon, maghrib at sunset and isha in the evening. From a raised place in the mosque, often a tower, the muezzin chants the call to prayer aloud. Think of it as a town clock that asks you to stop rather than hurry.

cards.headline: Wash, face, bow
cards.body: First comes wudu, washing the hands, face and feet, which is why mosques have washing facilities. Then the worshipper faces the qibla: the direction of the Kaaba, a cube-shaped shrine in Mecca's Great Mosque. In a mosque, a niche called the mihrab points the way. Each unit of prayer, a rakah, moves through standing, a bow and two prostrations, with "God is great" at every change of posture.

cards.headline: Alone, or shoulder to shoulder
cards.body: Muslims believe each worshipper speaks to God directly in prayer, with no priest in between; the imam who leads a mosque's prayers is not a priest. Muslims can pray anywhere, but praying together in a mosque is especially valued, rows side by side, as a sign that all are equal before God. On Friday the prayer just after noon becomes jumu'ah, a congregational prayer with two sermons from the pulpit.

cards.headline: Five Daily Prayers: the takeaways
learned: Muslims pray at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and evening
They wash first, then face the Kaaba in Mecca
On Friday the prayer after noon is prayed together, with sermons

questions.prompt: Which of the five daily prayers is said at sunset?
questions.explanation: Fajr at dawn, zuhr at midday, asr in the afternoon, maghrib at sunset, isha in the evening.

questions.prompt: How does a Muslim know which way to face for salat in a mosque?

options.label: Toward the rising sun, wherever the mosque is
options.rationale: The direction is Mecca, not the sun.

options.label: Toward the nearest minaret
options.rationale: The minaret is for the call to prayer.

options.label: Toward the Kaaba in Mecca, shown by the mihrab
Toward whichever wall the imam chooses
options.rationale: The qibla is fixed by the Kaaba's direction.

questions.explanation: Worshippers face the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca; a niche called the mihrab marks it.

questions.prompt: Level 34 put salat on a daily clock. How does that clock change on Friday?

options.label: The prayer after noon becomes a congregational one with sermons
All five prayers are skipped for a day of rest
options.rationale: Friday adds a gathering; it doesn't cancel prayer.

options.label: Prayer moves from five times to once a day
Only the dawn prayer is said, at home
options.rationale: Friday's special prayer is the one after noon, together.

questions.explanation: On Friday the prayer just after noon becomes jumu'ah, prayed together with two sermons.
